featured_reviews.name: Sachin Bhat
featured_reviews.review_text:
Known since 1700 AD, Matunga was a cluster of villages, which later on were brought under a single governing umbrella by the ruling British. The area was called Marubai Tekdi Gaon, which is said was shortened to MaTunGa (Matunga). Marubai is the traditional Gaondevi (village Goddess) of Matunga whose small temple existed under a peepal tree at King's Circle.

The then British Government planned to develop Bombay (Mumbai). Under the provisions of the City of Bombay Improvement Act, 1898, certain lands situated within the Island of Bombay were required for public purpose namely the Matunga Road Scheme, now the road is known as Dr. B. R. Ambedkar Road. So the authorities then decided to shift the Marubai temple from the Kings Circle peepal tree to a different location as it came in the way of the road building plan. However, they had to face tremendous opposition from the residents who feared they would invite the wrath of the Goddess if they shifted Her from Her original location.

The residents of the village then once again managed the new temple. In 1952 the Marubai Trust was formed under the Bombay Public Trust Act with Registration Number as “A2222(Mumbai)” .

Trustees
edit
The trustees managing the temple are descendants of those families who are managing the temple for last centuries. The First Trustee Shri. Kashinath Bhikaji Gavand was appointed in the same year. He was the father of present Managing Trustee Shri. Anil Gavand. After death of Shri. Kashinath Gavand, Shri. Anil Gavand was appointed the Managing Trustee in 1987.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Ganpati Bappa, also known as Ganesh Chaturthi, is a popular Hindu festival celebrated in honor of Lord Ganesha, the remover of obstacles. Here's a brief history:

- Pre-historic era: Ganesha worship dates back to the Indus Valley Civilization (3300-1300 BCE).

- Vedic period (1500 BCE - 500 BCE): Ganesha was mentioned in the Rigveda and other Vedic texts as a minor deity.

- Puranic period (500 BCE - 500 CE): Ganesha's popularity grew, and he became a prominent deity in Hindu mythology.

- 13th century CE: The festival of Ganesh Chaturthi was first celebrated in Maharashtra, India, during the reign of King Shivaji.

- 19th century CE: The festival gained popularity and spread to other parts of India, thanks to the efforts of Indian freedom fighter and social reformer Lokmanya Tilak.

- Present day: Ganesh Chaturthi is celebrated across India and globally, with millions of devotees worshiping Lord Ganesha for 10-11 days.

Some notable traditions and practices include:

- Installing clay idols of Ganesha in homes and public spaces
- Offering modaks (sweet dumplings) and other prasad
- Reciting prayers and performing pujas
- Immersing the idols in water bodies on the final day (Anant Chaturdashi)

Ganpati Bappa is a celebration of Lord Ganesha's wisdom, prosperity, and good fortune.

One of the iconic Ganpati to visit during Ganesh festivities. There are queues for Darshan. Volunteers are supportive and the line is fast moving. The ambience is divine. Be ready to wait for a while before getting the Darshan. Overall a great experience 👍👍👍

🏥Health and Hygiene - 4/5
👦 Kid friendly - Stay with kids as there  are chances of misplacing them
👫Staff - Volunteers are helpful
♿ Accessibility - Not accessible
🚾 Washrooms - Not sure
✅ Overall experience - 4/5

featured_reviews.name: Chandrakala Shetty
featured_reviews.review_text: Oh what a lovely place to be! Darshan can be taken without any hassles. The crowd here is really managed well. Even though there is a long queue but it doesn’t take that long to get Darshan. They have all the essential facilities available everywhere. Fans are put up everywhere. There are food counters and water stations around. Also when you get near the deity they do not push you or be in hurry. You can stand and pray at least.

featured_reviews.name: Rishu Bhosale
featured_reviews.review_text: Beautiful Ganesha Idol & an amazing job by all the people. I met people from abroad volunteering here. 10 days of absolute celebration, one should definitely have a glimpse of this Grand Festival.

featured_reviews.name: Ramya Iyer
featured_reviews.review_text: One of the top 5 and  ' must visit '  Sarvajanic Ganesh Utsav celebration in Mumbai. Preferably go on the first day of the festival. Its a 5-day Ganpati.

featured_reviews.name: Saurav
featured_reviews.review_text: Beautiful Ganpati Bappa Murti. It's an amazing experience here. The crowd is a lot, however the crowd management could be a bit better. Must visit.

featured_reviews.name: Roshni Kamath
featured_reviews.review_text: Mandatory visit on ganesh chaturthi. Feel blessed to see our Ganpati Bappa

featured_reviews.name: Shiv
featured_reviews.review_text: I've been visiting this place since over 10 years for Darshan & to seek blessings of Bappa almost every year. Very well organized & one can take proper Darshan and come out within 20 mins. Now ordering Sevas have become very easy & they are on-line. They email & whatsapp the receipt with QR code. Visit the place, scan QR, collect prasad. Very easy & convenient.
